observations.text: SP executed the formation take off as a wingman at the level expected for this training unit, with the IP directing the line up checks and calling the power setting at brake release. Position on the leader was kept during the T/O roll only while the IP prompted the throttle corrections, and the A/C configuration was cleaned after the leader's signal was pointed out from the front cockpit. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent execution of the line up checks and of the wingman power corrections is expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP, after the pre-flight study of the formation procedures, completed the line up checks and informed the formation leader, with verbal prompts from the IP required only for the trim setting. Position during the T/O roll was allowed to drift aft and the power correction was applied late, but it was made after the IP's call and no part of the take off had to be executed by the IP. The leader's signal was acknowledged and the A/C configuration was cleaned with delay, the climbout heading settling 10 degrees off the leader's before it was contained. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the line up checks without mistakes and informed the formation leader before lining up. Minor errors in power management left the A/C slightly aft of the briefed wingman position during the T/O roll, each one recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The leader's signals were followed and the configuration was cleaned in sequence, with airspeed on the climbout deviating by up to 15 knots from the briefed join speed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the line up checks without mistakes, informed the formation leader and set the briefed power in step with the leader at brake release. Proper position was kept throughout the T/O roll and the rotation, the leader's signals were followed promptly and the A/C configuration was cleaned in the correct sequence. Control of the A/C was smooth and accurate, with airspeed held within 10 knots and the climbout heading within 5 degrees of the leader's. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the formation take off as a wingman to the standards of the Techniques and Procedures Manual, the LAPs and the SOPs, with the line up checks completed and passed to the formation leader without any prompting. Position was held with negligible deviations through brake release, the T/O roll, the rotation and the cleanup, and the leader's signals were anticipated rather than merely followed. Control of the A/C was exceptionally smooth, leaving airspeed, heading and altitude deviations negligible throughout the join. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized line up flow, did not complete the line up checks before the leader's run-up signal and did not inform the formation leader, with the result that the IP had to direct the remaining items and set the take off power. Proper position was lost by more than two fuselage lengths on the T/O roll without a call to the leader, and the climbout heading diverged by more than 10 degrees from the leader's before the IP took the controls to re-establish the rejoin.

SP, due to failure to pass a required call at the briefed point, did not inform the leader timely when the A/C fell behind the briefed wingman position on the T/O roll, and pressed the correction with abrupt throttle inputs instead. Control of the A/C was not smooth and the airspeed overshoot on the join exceeded 20 knots, with the result that the IP took the controls and directed the rejoin. The leader's signal for cleanup was missed and the A/C configuration was cleaned only on the IP's command.

SP performed the formation take off within the standards expected for this training unit, completing the line up checks and the A/C cleanup after the IP's verbal indications. Deviation from the briefed wingman position on the T/O roll was recognized and corrected with delay, and the airspeed on the join reached 20 knots above the briefed value before it was contained. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timelier recognition of the position error and independent use of the line up flow are expected to improve.

SP executed the line up checks without mistakes and informed the formation leader before taxiing onto the runway. Small power corrections were needed to keep the proper position during the T/O roll, each one recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the leader's signal for cleanup was followed on time. Airspeed on the climbout deviated by up to 15 knots from the briefed join speed and the level-off altitude was held within 200 feet. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the formation take off as a wingman according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the SOPs, with the line up checks completed without mistakes and passed to the formation leader. Proper position was kept from brake release through the T/O roll and the rotation, and the A/C configuration was cleaned immediately on the leader's signal. Control of the A/C was smooth, with airspeed within 10 knots and the level-off altitude within 150 feet of the briefed values. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the formation take off with the accuracy and speed expected of a qualified wingman, completing the line up checks without mistakes and informing the formation leader without any prompting. Proper position was held with negligible deviations throughout the roll, the rotation and the cleanup, and every signal from the leader was acknowledged and executed without delay. Control inputs were smooth to the point that the airspeed, heading and altitude deviations on the join were negligible. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect throttle technique at brake release, did not set the briefed power in step with the leader and did not keep the proper position during the T/O roll, allowing the A/C to fall more than two fuselage lengths aft without informing the leader. The recovery input was abrupt, the airspeed overshot the briefed join speed by more than 20 knots and the climbout heading diverged by more than 10 degrees, with the result that the IP took the controls and directed the rejoin.

SP, due to attention captured by a single engine indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not follow the leader's signal to clean the A/C configuration and did not inform the leader of the delay. The gear and flaps were retracted only after the IP directed the action, and the A/C passed more than 300 feet above the briefed level-off altitude with a lateral drift that the IP had to correct on the controls.

SP, due to a non-standardized line up flow, did not execute the line up checks in the prescribed sequence and did not inform the formation leader until the IP prompted the call. Proper position on the T/O roll was allowed to drift aft and was corrected only after the IP's verbal indication, and the airspeed on the join reached 20 knots above the briefed value before it was contained. Errors were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in voicing a recognized inability to hold the briefed position, did not inform the leader timely that the wingman position on the T/O roll could not be kept with the power set. The correction followed only after the IP's verbal indication, and control of the A/C was not smooth, the level-off reaching 300 feet above the briefed altitude before it was contained. The leader's signal for the configuration cleanup was recognized and actioned with delay.

SP performed the formation take off within the desired standards, completing the line up checks without mistakes and informing the formation leader on time. However, keeping the proper position during the T/O roll required two power corrections of increasing size, each one recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the airspeed on the join deviated by up to 15 knots from the briefed value. Marginal performance for the Training Section - smoother power modulation on the roll is expected to improve position consistency in the following formation sorties.

SP executed the line up checks without mistakes, informed the formation leader and set the power accurately in step with the leader at brake release. Proper position was kept throughout the T/O roll and the rotation, the leader's signals were followed promptly and the A/C configuration was cleaned in the correct sequence. Control of the A/C was smooth, with airspeed held within 10 knots and the level-off altitude within 150 feet of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the formation take off as a wingman to a standard above that required at the end of the block, with the line up checks completed and passed to the formation leader without any prompting. Proper position was maintained with negligible deviations from brake release through the rotation and the cleanup, and each of the leader's signals was matched without perceptible lag. Control of the A/C was exceptionally smooth, leaving airspeed, heading and altitude deviations negligible on the join. Above end of block MIF achieved.
